title: Research: bounded diagonal sharing census over Dic3
body:
This package records a bounded exact test of whether noncommuting address words can share paid calls across three diagonal outputs. In the order-12 dicyclic algebra `F2[Dic_3]`, with exactly three registers, the charged alphabet `{u,v}`, and all 28 binary rank-one idempotents, no word of at most four calls realizes any of 1,482 monomial endpoint triples whose separate coordinate implementation costs at least five calls. One bounded depth-five pivot also finds no word for any of the 1,230 triples whose direct bill is at least six.

The meet-in-the-middle search is coefficientwise exact. It covers every product through depth two and three (2,409 and 94,727 distinct states); raw enumerations of all one/two-call and all three-call words confirm the state inventories. The package checks the group presentation, shortest positive-generator baseline, all paid-factor inverses, coordinate-word positive controls, noncommutative order and endpoint mutation controls. Reproduction:

```sh
python3.12 scripts/research_package.py --package research/bit-dicyclic-diagonal-seed620ca
```

This is a finite scoped negative result for the stated group, alphabet, endpoint family and depths. It does not establish a general nonabelian lower bound or a physical bit supplier, and it makes no new `kappa` claim. The selected result and its `kappa` remain unchanged. Assignment base: `fcea6916f3af98346ff13581ac7626718b7e55a2`; the branch is rebased on current `main`. Exact inputs and the selected-record hash are pinned in `SOURCES.json`.

The model is a specific nonabelian change to the scalar-idempotent framework studied by PR720 (head `a942c0ae1b463710ca535c1fba1b07b6431b5a86`) and its credited lineage. The search and package were prepared with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance.
